verdicts.reason: The Heading and Statement match the cited core statement: in TEI P5 4.12.0, anchor attaches an identifier to a point in a text, whether or not that point corresponds to a textual element. "Within a text" means the same as "in a text". The Support clause "It does not by itself establish identity across text versions" states a limitation, not a claimed source fact, so it adds no unsupported claim.

The Statement repeats the core statement word for word. It covers membership in att.global.responsibility and att.editLike, the cert, resp, evidence and source attributes, the purpose of giving more than one view when sources conflict, and the two birth-event example. The Heading's "for conflicting views" fairly condenses "in the case of multiple and conflicting sources more than one view... can be provided". The Support note only describes the passage and adds no new facts.

The Statement follows the core statement: information about a person, as distinct from references to a person such as by name, is grouped in person. personGrp 'may' be used for a group regarded as a single entity, such as an audience, and org 'should' be used for a group with a distinct identity, such as a named troupe. The modal verbs 'may' and 'should' are kept. The Heading covers only the first part, but it is accurate and does not claim to be complete. The Support entry is a bare citation with no added claims.

The Statement copies the core statement word for word, including the project-specific categories, the parallel with persons, the lack of any claim to comprehensiveness, the instruction that the generic state, trait and event elements 'should be used' and can be customized via type, and the extra elements population, climate and terrain. The Heading's 'recommends' and 'permits customization through type' fairly render 'should be used' and 'may be customized'. The Support entry is a bare citation.

The Statement copies the core statement word for word. It covers both reasons for using key without a direct link (a local convention, or the encoder judging that no resolution is needed) and both examples (a local database with project-specific identifiers built from the key value, and country or airport codes). The source's hedges 'might' and 'probably' are kept. The Heading accurately summarizes this. The Support entry is a bare citation.

The Heading and Statement match the core statement: in TEI P5 4.12.0, nym contains the definition for a canonical name or name component of any kind. The Support note's remark that the definition says nothing about nym's content model, class memberships or containing list element is a limitation, not a source claim, and it is consistent with the definition.

The Heading and Statement repeat the cited Core statement word for word: in TEI P5 4.12.0 the English description says persName contains a proper noun or proper-noun phrase referring to a person. The Support note only marks what the description leaves out (attributes, content model, other languages). It adds no factual claim that goes beyond the source.

The Statement keeps every element of the cited Guidelines statement: persName is repeatable within person, xml:lang gives the language and type the kind of name, the library 'base' or 'neutral' authority form is the contrast case, people resist foreign forms for local saints or heroes, any number of variants can be given with no prioritization, and the example uses Icelandic, Danish and Latin forms. Leaving out the Library of Congress example and 'less likelihood of offence' narrows nothing. The Heading's 'each with its language and kind' and the Support's 'decline a base form' are fair paraphrases of how the source describes typed, language-tagged repeats and its rejection of a base form. The Support's disclaimer about nyms adds no claim.

The Heading, Statement and cited Core statement all have the same scope: person provides information about an identifiable individual, for example a participant in a language interaction or a person referred to in a historical source. The Support note only lists topics the definition does not cover and adds no unsupported fact.

The Statement matches the cited Core statement in full: in testnames.xml, the record at block 137 has birth and death places made of settlement and country with neither type nor key, so the places are named but not identified, and an empty nationality element carries a key. The Heading's 'one record' is consistent with 'the record at block 137'. The Support line is only a link and adds no claim.

The March claim (make the repository private for now and reevaluate in Vancouver) matches the Würzburg minutes. 'The repository under discussion' correctly avoids naming it beyond the sandbox-repository item. The May claim (the P6 sandbox repository will be kept private for now while linked from the minutes) matches the 20 May discussion and is correctly placed within the Council discussion. 'Temporary' in the Heading is a fair reading of 'for now'. The assertion explicitly declines to claim the two repositories are the same, that access stayed private in between, or anything about visibility after May, so it makes no unsupported joint inference.

The DraCor clause matches the cited constraint, including the root rule, role="warning", the two alternatives and the dracor.org/schema.rng reference. 'Embeds Schematron reports in its change to gap' matches the cited embedded Schematron rule that reports on gap. The correspSearch clause matches the service running schxslt:validate against cmif.sch alongside validation:jing-report against cmi-customization.rng. 'Separately named' only notes that it is a distinct file. Omitting the geonames check and view.xsl narrows nothing. The stated limits on runtime behaviour and on the CMIF ODD avoid overreach.

The ground is cited only for the SZDMSK.3 sentence. It states the same thing: entry SZDMSK.3 has a term with type="work" and ref="#SZDWRK.2". The SZDMSK.4 claim is attributed to ^s5, and the shared-reference heading is a joint inference judged separately.

The sentence attributed to ^s5, "The commenter wrote that this can be seen from their spec files," matches the core statement. It is correctly attributed to a commenter in issue 2739. The membership claims belong to ^s4.

The sentence attributed to ^s6, "They gave the URL of the att.personal specification file on the repository's dev branch," matches the core statement, including the dev-branch detail. The membership claims are attributed to ^s4.

The statement repeats the core statement almost word for word. It keeps the November 2011 Paris Council framing, the attribution to the issue author, the "we will modify" announcement wording, the interim nature of the change and the switch from key to ref. It reports only an announcement, not an actual change to the Guidelines.

Block 44 says that head marks "a heading prefixed to the start of any textual division" and that "A given division may contain more than one such element." Its Etymology example has two consecutive head elements at the start of a div1.

Block 45 says that "the type or level of heading intended is implied by the immediate parent of the head element." It also says that "the encoder may choose to extend the model.headLike class ... to include other such elements if required." The statement matches both points.

Block 84 says that quote's semantics "suggest that its content derives from a source external to the current text." It says floatingText "carries no such implication" and is used "whenever the richer content model that it provides is required" for a part of a text "presented as a discrete 'inclusion.'" The statement matches this contrast.

Block 99 says that figure can appear in titlePage along with model.titlepagePart elements. It says figure is included "to enable encoders to record the presence of complex non-textual material on a title page." For "simple cases such as printers' ornaments or illustrations the graphic element ... should be adequate." Calling that a suggestion is a fair paraphrase.

Block 105 gives two possible approaches to title-page rendition. The first: "One approach ... would be to use the seg tag ... and then use the global rend attribute." The second: "Another would be to use a module specialized for the description of typographic entities." The statement calls these possible approaches, which matches the source's conditional wording ("would be").

Block 26 contains every part of the statement. It says rs and name "can distinguish names in a text but are insufficiently powerful to mark their internal components or structure." It says that for "nominal record linkage or even to create an alphabetically sorted list of personal names, it is important to distinguish between a family name, a forename and an honorary title." Its specList provides persName, surname, forename, roleName, addName, nameLink and genName "for these and related purposes." The version attribution matches the source metadata (4.12.0).
Block 67 (/classSpec/attList/attDef[5]/desc[1]) sits under attDef ident="next" and reads verbatim: "points to the next element of a virtual aggregate of which the current element is part."

Reading 6, the English remarks paragraph p[4] on attDef source, states: "when used on other elements multiple values are permitted." The condition is preserved, and the statement makes no claim about the one-value rule for schema components.

Reading 1 (classSpec desc[1]) reads: "common attributes for those elements which form part of a name usually, but not necessarily, a personal name." The quoted qualifier matches exactly and applies to the name.
Reading 2 (attDef[@ident='full']/desc[1]) reads verbatim: "indicates whether the name component is given in full, as an abbreviation or simply as an initial."

Block 4 (p[3]) says that because TEI can be a child of itself, an outermost TEI element with a teiHeader holding collection-level metadata contains a complete TEI element for each document. Each of those has its own teiHeader with metadata for that document.
Block 9 (p[8]) reads: "In unitary texts, the text body is tagged body; in composite texts, where the text body consists of a series of subordinate texts or groups, it is tagged group."

The ground supports the March 2026 clause: the Würzburg minutes, under continued support of P5 while developing P6, list announcing at the Annual Members' Meeting that new features stop until P6 starts. The assertion's label for this record, 'a planned announcement', fits it, and the assertion does not say the announcement was made or carried out. The other dated positions belong to other grounds.

This ground's part is the CMIF clause, 'the CMIF ODD carries no `source` attribute on its `schemaSpec`'. The distillate says directly that the cmi-customization schemaSpec carries no source attribute. The DraCor and EpiDoc values are attributed to other sources, and the assertion's limitation is about scope, not a claim about the source.
All four methods match the distillate. 'Boundary marking' is a faithful paraphrase of 'empty boundary elements', and the version (4.12.0) and purpose (handling non-hierarchical information) are kept.

The distillate names maintenance of repeated textual content and the lack of explicit relations between views as disadvantages of multiple encoding in the 4.12.0 chapter. The assertion repeats only those disadvantages and leaves out the advantages without misstating them.

The statement repeats the distillate almost word for word and keeps both conditions (numbered in sequence, reconstructable by software) and the hedge 'may well be considered unnecessary'. The heading keeps the conditions too, as 'sequential' and 'when software can reconstruct them'.

The distillate records that issue 1400's labels at the 2026-09-06 snapshot include reconsideration for P6. The assertion is limited to that same snapshot and claims only that the label was present, nothing about the outcome.

Reading 3 is located at attDef[@ident='active']/desc. It reads: "identifies the active participants in a non-mutual relationship, or all the participants in a mutual one." That matches the statement's condition (a mutual relationship) and its content (identifies all participants), and the source is TEI P5 4.12.0.

Reading 5 is located at attDef[@ident='passive']/desc, the English description in the relation elementSpec. It reads: "identifies the passive participants in a non-mutual relationship." The statement repeats this wording.

Block 34 reads: <person xml:id="CarLun01" sex="1" role="binder" rend="nolist"> <persName xml:lang="da">Carl Lund</persName>. So rend sits on the person element alongside xml:id, sex and role, and the contained persName has only xml:lang.

Block 120 has <birth notBefore="1651" notAfter="1671">c. 1661</birth>: the dates are twenty years apart and "c." marks the year as approximate. It also has <death notBefore="1742" notAfter="1742">1742</death>, which uses the same attribute pair with identical values. The claim that one mechanism expresses both a range and a point follows directly from these two encodings.

The complete statement matches the cited distillate statement word for word. That includes the project-specific categories, the explicit disclaimer of comprehensiveness, the generic state/trait/event elements that can be customized through @type, and the predefined population, climate and terrain elements. The heading's word "recommends" fairly paraphrases "should be used", and "permits customization through type" matches "may be customized ... by means of its type attribute".

The statement repeats the cited description of @source in att.global.source for version 4.12.0: it specifies the source from which some aspect of this element is drawn. Calling att.global.source an "attribute class" adds no new factual claim.

The statement repeats the cited English description of state in 4.12.0. It keeps the hedge "often" and both conditions, "at some specific time or for a specific date range". The added phrase "it describes" only restates whose status or quality is meant and does not overreach.

The statement matches the cited distillate word for word. It names the same document (testnames.xml), the same location (block 84) and the same details: a note stating a spouse relation, containing a name with type="person", a nonempty key and no ref. The heading leaves out the block number, but it makes no claim the source doesn't support.

This ground supports the March part of the assertion: the Würzburg minutes record a Council decision to make the repository private "for now" and to reevaluate at the Vancouver face-to-face meeting. The assertion keeps both the temporary condition and the reevaluation condition. It calls this simply "the repository under discussion" and explicitly declines to identify it with the May P6 sandbox, so this ground isn't stretched. The 20 May claim is attributed to another source.

This ground supports the March part of the assertion: under "establishing a workspace" in the next-steps planning, the Würzburg minutes list creating a sandbox repository, and the assertion describes that as a listed next step. The claim that work is proceeding in TEIC/p6-sandbox comes from the separately attributed minutes of 24 April 2026. The assertion does not claim that this ground named the repository or that it was created in March.

Block 39 says addName and roleName mark 'all name components other than those already listed'. It says roleName encloses a title 'which exists in some sense independently of its bearer' and that 'The distinction is not always a clear one.' It says contextual roles such as witness or defendant should not use roleName, because roleName marks 'roles which function as part of a person's name'. It also says roles and occupations are encoded within person. Every clause of the statement is covered.

Block 47 calls the orgName encoding 'equivalent to, but more specific than, either of the following representations' (rs and name). It describes the key attribute (external identifier such as a database key) and the ref attribute (points to an org element). It says type 'should be used to characterize the name (rather than the organization)', with acronym, phrase and composite examples. The statement matches.

Block 93 says 'These elements may appear only within a listPerson element, which groups such descriptions together, and optionally also describes relationships amongst the people listed.' Its specList names listPerson and listRelation. Here 'these elements' means person and personGrp from Block 92, so 'these person descriptions' is a fair paraphrase.

Block 144 says the modern and Roman city 'are not physically co-extensive, they have significant areas which overlap, and we may therefore wish to regard them as the same place, while supplying both names with an indication of the time period during which each was current.' The statement keeps the 'may wish' wording, so the claim is not strengthened.

Block 5 says that in its examples it restricts itself to 'metrical lines and line groups' for the Metrical View and to 'sentences' for the Grammatical View. For the Dialogic View it will 'only ... distinguish direct quotation from other narration'. The statement accurately reflects this limit, which applies to the worked examples.

Block 20 says that if the custom elements 'can be replaced by TEI elements and attributes without loss of information, this method is TEI-conformant'. It says that if they 'introduce information or distinctions that cannot be captured using standard TEI elements, the method is an extension.' Both conditions are kept, and Block 19 confirms the method is the custom boundary elements.
Reading block r2 gives the revisionDesc change exactly: when="2026-01-26" with the text "release 9.8: Aligned schema with TEI v. 4.10.2". The date and the wording both match.

Block r4 says "as a matter of policy the EpiDoc schema should be a conformant subset of the latest TEI schema (only exceptions being when the dev TEI ODD contains changes that will not make it into the TEI release for 1-6 months)". The statement paraphrases this accurately and keeps both the policy framing and the exception condition.

Block r2 shows <licence target="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">Licensed under a Creative Commons-Attribution 4.0 licence.</licence>. Both the target and the licence text match the statement.

Block r6 is the div with type="edition", subtype="primary" and xml:lang="la". It contains expan/abbr/ex for D(is) and M(anibus), supplied reason="lost", g ref="#ivy-leaf", and gap reason="lost" extent="unknown" unit="character". Every element named in the statement is present.

Reading 7 is the English remarks paragraph p[1] of the 4.12.0 att.editLike spec. It says members "are typically used to represent any kind of editorial intervention in a text, for example a correction or interpretation". The statement drops the trailing "or to date or localize manuscripts etc.", but leaving that out does not distort what the paragraph says.
Reading 8 is the English remarks paragraph p[2] of the 4.12.0 att.editLike spec. Its wording matches the statement, including the "(if present)" condition and the examples witness, msDesc and bibl.

Both claims match their grounds and keep the 4.12.0 version. Claim 1 correctly restates ^s38: when the module is included, listRelation/relation may document relationships 'amongst the persons, places or organizations identified', and name, active, mutual and passive are selected for documentation. It also correctly restates ^s39, where a participant 'might be a person, a place or an organization'. Leaving out the att.typed detail does not distort anything. Claim 2 copies the relation specification's English description (^s2) word for word: 'places, events, persons, objects or other items'. The two claims are about the same version, so the tension is not about dates. It is about levels: the chapter prose about this module's scope lists persons, places and organizations, while the element-level description lists a wider, open-ended set (events, objects, other items) and does not mention organizations. Both claims keep the hedged wording ('might be', 'other items'), so the documented difference is shown faithfully and not resolved.

Claim 1 matches the att.canonical 4.12.0 remarks (^s4) almost word for word: no particular syntax is proposed because the form 'will depend entirely on practice within a given project'. Claim 2 keeps the attribution in ^s4 of the issue distillate: it is the issue author who 'reported as the Council's vision' a wish to deprecate key 'some day', held back by how widely key was used. The past tense and 'at the time of writing' tie it to the 2011-11-13 issue description, so it does not state an actual Council decision or an actual deprecation.
